subject: Urology
title: Urinary Tract Infection
subtitle: Definitions, acute cystitis, acute pyelonephritis, urosepsis, schistosomiasis and genitourinary tuberculosis
sourceNote: Built only from the uploaded URINARY TRACT INFECTION 1(2) lecture. The bank preserves the lecture terminology, thresholds, drug doses, timings and treatment statements without replacing them with external guidelines.

cases.title: Classifying a Recurrent Urinary Infection
cases.scenario: A patient has had three documented urinary infections during the last 12 months. The urinary tract is structurally and functionally normal, and the previous episode was four months ago.
cases.ar: مريض حصل له 3 urinary infections خلال آخر 12 شهر، والurinary tract طبيعي structurally وfunctionally، وآخر مرة كانت من 4 شهور.
questions: Define urinary tract infection and significant bacteriuria.
Classify this infection as uncomplicated or complicated.
Is the pattern isolated or recurrent? State the lecture criteria.
Name the two mechanisms of recurrent UTI listed in the lecture.
answer: UTI is infection of any part of the urinary system. Significant bacteriuria is considered when urine culture reveals more than 10^5 colonies/ml.
It is an uncomplicated UTI because the urinary tract is structurally and functionally normal.
It is recurrent UTI: more than two infections in six months or three within twelve months. An isolated UTI requires an interval of at least six months.
Reinfection or bacterial persistence.
cases.trap: Do not call it isolated when the interval is shorter than six months.

cases.title: Pyuria Without Bacteriuria
cases.scenario: Urinalysis shows more than 5 white blood cells per high-power field, but urine culture does not demonstrate bacteriuria.
cases.ar: الurinalysis فيه WBCs أكتر من 5/HPF لكن الurine culture مفيهوش bacteriuria.
questions: What is pyuria according to the lecture?
What is this specific finding called?
List the causes of this finding mentioned in the lecture.
What may bacteriuria without pyuria indicate?
answer: Pyuria is the presence of white blood cells in urine, more than 5 WBC/HPF.
Sterile pyuria.
Carcinoma in situ, tuberculosis infection and bladder stones.
It may indicate bacterial colonization rather than active infection.
cases.trap: Sterile pyuria means pyuria without bacteriuria.

cases.title: Typical Acute Cystitis
cases.scenario: A young woman presents with frequency, urgency, nocturia, dysuria, suprapubic pain and hematuria without features of upper urinary tract infection.
cases.ar: سيدة شابة عندها frequency وurgency وnocturia وdysuria مع suprapubic pain وhematuria من غير علامات upper UTI.
questions: What is the most likely diagnosis?
Why is the condition more common in females according to the lecture?
What is honeymoon cystitis?
Does every simple case require urine culture?
answer: Acute cystitis.
Because of the short female urethra, making ascending infection easier.
Cystitis after sexual activity in early marriage.
No. Simple cystitis does not require urine culture.
cases.trap: The lecture specifically says simple cystitis does not routinely require culture.

cases.title: Cystitis Requiring Urine Culture
cases.scenario: A pregnant woman has symptoms of cystitis. Another patient has symptoms that recur within four weeks after treatment.
cases.ar: حامل عندها أعراض cystitis، ومريض تاني الأعراض رجعت خلال 4 أسابيع بعد العلاج.
questions: Is urine culture indicated in these patients?
List all indications for urine culture in simple cystitis stated in the lecture.
Outline the treatment of acute cystitis.
Which antibiotic group is excluded in pregnancy and lactation according to the lecture?
answer: Yes, urine culture is indicated.
Pregnancy, suspected acute pyelonephritis, and symptoms that do not resolve or recur within four weeks.
Plenty of water, a short antibiotic course such as nitrofurantoin 100 mg twice daily or fluoroquinolones, plus antispasmodics and analgesics.
Fluoroquinolones.
cases.trap: Preserve the lecture exclusion of fluoroquinolones in pregnancy and lactation.
cases.memory: Culture: pregnancy, pyelo suspicion, persistent/recurrent within 4 weeks.

cases.title: Classic Acute Pyelonephritis
cases.scenario: A patient has high-grade fever, chills, rigors, flank pain, dysuria, flank tenderness and pyuria.
cases.ar: مريض عنده high-grade fever وchills وrigors مع flank pain وdysuria، والفحص فيه flank tenderness والurine فيه pyuria.
questions: What is the diagnosis?
Define the condition.
State the routes of infection.
What triad is described as pathognomonic in the lecture?
What initial investigations are required?
answer: Acute pyelonephritis.
Acute inflammation of the renal pelvis and renal parenchyma.
Ascending, hematogenous and lymphatic spread.
Fever, flank tenderness and pyuria.
Urinalysis and culture for every case, CBC, and abdominal ultrasound.
cases.trap: The lecture requires urinalysis and culture in every pyelonephritis case.
cases.memory: Pyelo triad: fever + flank tenderness + pyuria.

cases.title: Unexplained High Fever in a Child
cases.scenario: A child presents with high-grade fever without a clear cause and without the classic adult manifestations.
cases.ar: طفل عنده high-grade fever من غير سبب واضح ومفيش الclassic adult manifestations.
questions: What diagnosis must be excluded?
Why can diagnosis be difficult in children according to the lecture?
Which urine investigations should be performed if pyelonephritis is suspected?
answer: UTI must be excluded.
The classic manifestations are often absent in children.
Urinalysis and urine culture.
cases.trap: A child may lack classic manifestations; unexplained high fever still requires exclusion of UTI.
cases.memory: Child + unexplained high fever = exclude UTI.

cases.title: Pyelonephritis Not Improving After 72 Hours
cases.scenario: A hospitalized patient with acute pyelonephritis receives treatment but fails to improve after 72 hours.
cases.ar: مريض محجوز بسبب acute pyelonephritis ومتحسنش بعد 72 ساعة.
questions: Which imaging study is indicated at this point?
List the complications of acute pyelonephritis given in the lecture.
Outline the treatment plan.
How should antibiotics be adjusted?
answer: CT scan.
Renal or perirenal abscesses, papillary necrosis and chronic pyelonephritis.
Hospitalization, bed rest, intravenous fluids, analgesic-antipyretic treatment and parenteral broad-spectrum empirical antibiotics.
Start with a parenteral third-generation cephalosporin, then shift to a suitable antibiotic according to culture.
cases.trap: The lecture specifies CT when there is no improvement within 72 hours.

cases.title: Urosepsis with HAT Signs
cases.scenario: A patient with pyelonephritis becomes hypotensive with systolic blood pressure of 95 mmHg, develops an altered mental state and has a respiratory rate of 24/min.
cases.ar: مريض pyelonephritis ضغطه systolic 95، وحصل altered mental state والrespiratory rate بقى 24/min.
questions: What is the diagnosis?
What does HAT stand for and what thresholds are stated?
Why is this condition dangerous?
What specialists are required?
answer: Urosepsis.
Hypotension: systolic BP 100 mmHg or less; Altered mental state; Tachypnea: respiratory rate 22/min or more.
The exaggerated immune response may cause multiple-organ damage; sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction with high mortality.
A urologist and an ICU specialist.
cases.trap: The source uses HAT as the bedside remembrance tool.

cases.title: Immediate Emergency Management of Urosepsis
cases.scenario: Urosepsis is clinically suspected in the emergency department before culture results are available.
cases.ar: في الemergency فيه clinical suspicion of urosepsis ولسه نتائج الculture مظهرتش.
questions: List the immediate actions in sequence.
Which samples are required?
Should empirical antibiotics wait for culture results?
Why is time crucial?
answer: Give oxygen by mask, start intravenous fluids, take urine and blood samples for culture, begin high-dose empirical antibiotics, and request a urologist and ICU specialist.
Urine and blood samples for culture.
No; empirical antibiotics should be started immediately in high dose.
Urosepsis is an emergency and the time to start treatment is crucial.
cases.trap: Cultures are taken, but treatment is not delayed while awaiting results.
cases.memory: O2 + IV fluids + urine/blood cultures + high-dose antibiotics + ICU/urology.

cases.title: Septic Shock Requiring Vasopressors
cases.scenario: A patient with sepsis requires vasopressors to maintain the blood pressure target stated in the lecture.
cases.ar: مريض sepsis محتاج vasopressors علشان يحافظ على هدف الضغط المذكور في المحاضرة.
questions: What is this condition called?
Define it exactly as stated in the lecture.
What is the most frequent cause of urosepsis?
answer: Septic shock.
A subset of sepsis in which the patient requires vasopressors to maintain systolic blood pressure at or above 60 mmHg.
Pyelonephritis.
cases.trap: This answer intentionally preserves the numerical statement used in the uploaded lecture.

cases.title: Early Genitourinary Schistosomiasis
cases.scenario: A patient reports swimmer’s itch followed later by terminal hematuria.
cases.ar: مريض بدأ عنده swimmer’s itch وبعدها ظهر terminal hematuria.
questions: What is the likely diagnosis?
State the three clinical stages.
Describe the basic pathological sequence around deposited eggs.
What is the drug of choice?
answer: Genitourinary schistosomiasis (bilharzia).
Initial stage: swimmer’s itch; acute stage: terminal hematuria; stage of complications.
Eggs are deposited in small venules; granulomas form around them and are gradually replaced by collagen, resulting in fibrosis.
Praziquantel.
cases.trap: Terminal hematuria is the acute-stage manifestation highlighted by the lecture.

cases.title: Complicated Bilharzial Urinary Disease
cases.scenario: A patient with chronic bilharzia develops a contracted bladder, ureteric obstruction with hydronephrosis and hemospermia.
cases.ar: مريض chronic bilharzia ظهر عنده contracted bladder وureteric obstruction مع hydronephrosis وكمان hemospermia.
questions: Classify the bladder lesions into atrophic and hypertrophic groups.
Explain the ureteric complication.
Explain the genital manifestation.
List the investigations stated in the lecture.
answer: Atrophic lesions: ulcerations and contracted bladder. Hypertrophic lesions: hyperplasia, metaplasia, dysplasia, polyposis and carcinoma.
Ureteral stricture causes hydroureter and hydronephrosis.
Hemospermia results from seminal-vesicle involvement.
Urine analysis, serological tests, abdominal ultrasound, KUB and CT.
cases.trap: Do not omit carcinoma from the hypertrophic bladder complications.
cases.memory: Bilharzia complications: bladder fibrosis/tumor, ureteric stricture, hemospermia.

cases.title: Praziquantel Regimen
cases.scenario: A patient is diagnosed with genitourinary schistosomiasis and requires specific medical treatment.
cases.ar: مريض اتشخص genitourinary schistosomiasis ومحتاج specific medical treatment.
questions: Name the drug of choice.
State the total dose.
How is the dose divided and spaced?
What additional principle is stated after medical treatment?
answer: Praziquantel.
60 mg/kg.
Three divided doses, six hours apart.
Treatment of complications is also required.
cases.trap: Remember the lecture regimen exactly: 60 mg/kg in three doses six hours apart.

cases.title: Sterile Pyuria with Renal Cavities
cases.scenario: A patient has microscopic hematuria, sterile pyuria, lower urinary tract symptoms and imaging showing hydronephrosis with renal cavities.
cases.ar: مريض عنده microscopic hematuria وsterile pyuria وLUTS، والimaging فيه hydronephrosis وrenal cavities.
questions: What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which organs are the primary sites?
Which test is essential for diagnosis?
List the imaging findings and studies in the lecture.
answer: Genitourinary tuberculosis.
The kidney and epididymis, with later spread to the ureter and bladder.
PCR.

Ultrasound may show hydronephrosis and renal cavities; KUB may show calcification in the renal parenchyma and GU tract; CT may show hydronephrosis and/or contracted bladder; chest X-ray assesses pulmonary disease.
cases.trap: Sterile pyuria is a key clue, but PCR is described as essential.
cases.memory: GU TB: sterile pyuria + PCR + cavities/calcification.

cases.title: Epididymal Tuberculosis with Discharging Sinus
cases.scenario: A patient has painful scrotal swelling, a posterior discharging sinus and a beaded vas. Medical therapy does not cure the sinus.
cases.ar: مريض عنده painful scrotal swelling مع posterior discharging sinus وbeaded vas، والmedical treatment مش مخلص الsinus.
questions: What is the diagnosis and involved organ?
Describe the standard multidrug regimen.
What operation is indicated if the sinus persists?
When is nephrectomy indicated in genitourinary TB?
answer: Epididymal involvement by genitourinary tuberculosis.
Rifampicin, INH and pyrazinamide for the first two months, followed by rifampicin and INH for four more months.
Epididymectomy.
For a non-functioning kidney.
cases.trap: Surgery is reserved for the lecture indications; multidrug anti-TB therapy remains the cornerstone.
cases.memory: Persistent TB sinus = epididymectomy; nonfunctioning kidney = nephrectomy.

coreShorts.q: Define urinary tract infection.
coreShorts.a: Infection of any part of the urinary system.

coreShorts.q: Define significant bacteriuria according to the lecture.
coreShorts.a: Urine culture showing more than 10^5 colonies/ml.

coreShorts.q: Define pyuria and state the microscopic threshold.
coreShorts.a: Presence of WBCs in urine; more than 5 WBC/HPF.

coreShorts.q: Define sterile pyuria and list its causes in the lecture.
a: Causes: carcinoma in situ, tuberculosis and bladder stones.

coreShorts.q: Differentiate uncomplicated from complicated UTI.
a: Uncomplicated UTI occurs in a structurally and functionally normal urinary tract.
Complicated UTI occurs with an underlying anatomical or functional abnormality.

coreShorts.q: State the criteria for recurrent UTI.
coreShorts.a: More than two infections in six months or three within twelve months.

coreShorts.q: Differentiate isolated UTI, recurrent UTI and unresolved infection.
a: Isolated: at least six months between infections.

coreShorts.q: Define acute cystitis and explain why it is more common in females.
a: The female urethra is short, making ascending infection easier.

coreShorts.q: What is honeymoon cystitis?
coreShorts.a: Cystitis after sexual activity in early marriage.

coreShorts.q: Enumerate the symptoms of acute cystitis.
State the indications for urine culture in simple cystitis.
a: Symptoms that fail to resolve or recur within four weeks.

coreShorts.q: Outline treatment of acute cystitis.
a: Short antibiotic course: nitrofurantoin 100 mg twice daily or fluoroquinolones, excluding pregnancy and lactation.

coreShorts.q: Define acute pyelonephritis and list routes of infection.
a: Acute inflammation of renal pelvis and parenchyma.

coreShorts.q: State the clinical picture of acute pyelonephritis.
What triad is described as pathognomonic for acute pyelonephritis?
What is the important pediatric note about UTI?
coreShorts.a: Classic manifestations may be absent; high-grade fever without a clear cause requires exclusion of UTI.

coreShorts.q: List investigations for acute pyelonephritis.
a: Urinalysis and culture for every case.
CT if there is no improvement within 72 hours.

coreShorts.q: List complications of acute pyelonephritis.
coreShorts.a: Renal/perirenal abscesses, papillary necrosis and chronic pyelonephritis.

coreShorts.q: Outline treatment of acute pyelonephritis.
a: Parenteral broad-spectrum empirical antibiotic such as third-generation cephalosporin, then culture-directed therapy.

coreShorts.q: Define urosepsis and state its commonest cause.
a: Urosepsis occurs when organisms causing UTI invade the bloodstream and the immune response may cause organ damage.
Pyelonephritis is the most frequent cause.

coreShorts.q: What are the HAT signs of sepsis?
List immediate management steps for suspected urosepsis.
Define septic shock as stated in the lecture.
coreShorts.a: Sepsis requiring vasopressors to maintain systolic blood pressure ≥60 mmHg.

coreShorts.q: Name the two specific urinary infections covered in the lecture.
Describe the pathological sequence in genitourinary schistosomiasis.
coreShorts.a: Egg deposition in small venules → granuloma formation → collagen replacement → fibrosis.

coreShorts.q: State the three clinical stages of genitourinary schistosomiasis.
Enumerate bladder complications of schistosomiasis.
a: Hypertrophic: hyperplasia, metaplasia, dysplasia, polyposis and carcinoma.

coreShorts.q: State ureteric and genital complications of schistosomiasis.
a: Ureteral stricture causing hydroureter and hydronephrosis.

coreShorts.q: List investigations for genitourinary schistosomiasis.
coreShorts.a: Urine analysis, serological tests, abdominal ultrasound, KUB and CT.

coreShorts.q: State the praziquantel regimen in the lecture.
coreShorts.a: 60 mg/kg in three divided doses six hours apart.

coreShorts.q: State the primary sites and spread pattern of genitourinary TB.
coreShorts.a: Kidney and epididymis are primary sites; infection then spreads to ureter and bladder.

coreShorts.q: Enumerate the clinical features of genitourinary TB.
a: Epididymal disease: painful scrotal swelling, posterior discharging sinus and beaded vas.

coreShorts.q: List investigations for genitourinary TB.
a: US, KUB, CT and chest X-ray with the findings stated in the lecture.

coreShorts.q: State the anti-TB drug regimen.
coreShorts.a: Rifampicin, INH and pyrazinamide for two months, then rifampicin and INH for four months.

coreShorts.q: State the surgical indications in genitourinary TB.
a: Epididymectomy when medical treatment fails to cure a discharging sinus.
